universalAnswers.whatHappened: New York City announced a one-school-year pause on student-facing generative AI in public-school early-childhood programs through eighth grade on September 2; students returned September 10 under the current guidance.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: Student-facing generative AI is software a student directly uses that creates text, images, audio or other content from instructions.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: The September 2 Mayor’s Office announcement, current NYCPS guidance and family notice, and complete Associated Press article body were reviewed through September 11.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: The policy and pilot criteria are government records. The current software-review process checks privacy and security; NYCPS says broader bias, equity and instructional-effectiveness evaluation capacity is still being built. Independent reporting supplies criticism, not implementation findings.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: A child in a reader’s family may be assigned a school tool, receive a grade or placement decision, or rely on assistive or language-access technology.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: Students, families and staff in New York City public schools during the 2026–27 school year; younger grades, high school and students using necessary accessibility tools have different rules.
universalAnswers.changesNow: Student-facing generative AI is paused in early-childhood programs through eighth grade; high-school use is limited; staff may use approved AI for planning and operations but not for grading, behavior monitoring or consequential student decisions.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: School-by-school implementation, pilot learning results, broader bias/effectiveness evaluation and the policy after 2026–27 remain unresolved.
universalAnswers.readerAction: For a specific school tool, current guidance names the school principal; concerns can also go to the school, School Leadership Team or Community Education Council.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: Who is using the AI, what decision can it influence, and what did the approval process actually test?

legal-policy.legalStatus: This is a New York City Public Schools policy for the 2026–27 school year, announced September 2 and reflected in current guidance; it is not described as a national law.
legal-policy.jurisdiction: The reviewed rules govern New York City public-school use, including specified school-hour and school-building programs; they do not set a nationwide or household rule.
legal-policy.parties: The Mayor’s Office and NYC Public Schools announced and administer the policy; students, families, staff, schools and approved vendors have different roles.
legal-policy.allegationVsFinding: NYCPS states its reasons and intended learning safeguards. AP reports outside concerns. Neither source establishes school-by-school compliance or that approved pilots improve learning.
legal-policy.currentEffect: For 2026–27, early-childhood programs through eighth grade may not use student-facing generative AI; approved supervised high-school uses and necessary accessibility/language tools remain; staff face decision-use restrictions.
legal-policy.unresolvedQuestions: Implementation consistency, pilot outcomes, broader tool evaluation and future-year policy remain open.
legal-policy.nextMilestone: The Technology in Schools Coalition plans an April 2027 policy-recommendations report.

translation.newsVersionExact: New York City announced on September 2 that its public schools would pause student-facing generative AI from early-childhood programs through eighth grade for the 2026–27 school year.
translation.actualMeaningExact: The boundary is narrower than “AI is banned in school.”
translation.mechanismExact: Teachers and staff may use approved AI for planning and operational tasks. They may not use it for grading, behavior monitoring, placement, promotion, graduation or other decisions about students.
translation.familiarExampleExact: A teacher may use an approved tool to help plan a lesson, but cannot let it assign a student’s grade or placement.
